items.summary: Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal on Tuesday launched a critique of the administrative functioning of the higher judiciary, warning that the "master of the roster" system, backroom bargaining within the Collegium and complete opacity surrounding in-house disciplinary inquiries against judges accused of misbehaviour have triggered a crisis of public confidence. Sibal was speaking at a discussion organised by the Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reforms (CJAR) at the India International Centre in New Delhi. He observed that while judicial pronouncements are publicly debated, the unreviewable administrative discretion of Chief Justices has left the judicial institution vulnerable to systemic erosion. "There is a public debate on the judicial side of judgments of the court. But there can't be a debate within the public on decisions which are administrative. I can't criticise a judge for fixing a matter, or Chief Justice for fixing a matter before another judge," he said. He went on to note that ultimately, a judge is only answerable to his own conscience in such matters. " How do we get accountability into the system? You know, as a human being, at the end of the day, you're accountable to your conscience. That is the real accountability. And we are all human beings; even judges are human beings. items.title: Kerala Congress tenders unconditional apology to CJI Surya Kant over tweet calling for resignation
items.summary: The Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) has tendered an unconditional apology to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant over a tweet effectively calling for his resignation. The apology was submitted by KPCC President Sunny Joseph in a formal reply dated October 22 to a legal notice issued by Supreme Court lawyer and Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) Joint Secretary Meenesh Dubey. Dubey had threatened to initiate criminal contempt of court proceedings after a post appeared on October 12 from the official X handle (@INCKerala) stating: "Dear Surya Kant, If law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it." In his reply, Joseph clarified that the post was drafted and published by party worker Vijay Thottathil without the leadership's knowledge, consent, or consultation. Joseph confirmed that Thottathil had been immediately stripped of his responsibilities and was instructed to issue a public apology. "The demand for resignation and the suggestion of finding a replacement for the Hon’ble Chief Justice were inappropriate and should not have appeared on an official party platform...On its behalf, I tender an unconditional apology to the Hon'ble Chief Justice of India for the publication and the disrespect conveyed by its language," the KPCC President stated. The State Congress chief emphasised that while political expression is protected in a democracy, it does not absolve organisations of the duty to maintain institutional dignity. Joseph noted that political disagreement cannot justify language that undermines constitutional offices. Addressing concerns regarding evidence tampering and systemic lapses, the KPCC confirmed that an internal inquiry has been initiated to overhaul its digital oversight protocols noting that external agencies assist with account handling. The committee assured that all relevant electronic records, device access logs and communications would be preserved in accordance with the law. The party also undertook to publish its official clarification and apology on its public social media channels.

items.title: CAT slams Railway officials for twisting former Solicitor General's undertaking to Supreme Court
items.summary: The Jaipur bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) has criticised railway officials for attempting to circumvent an undertaking given by former Solicitor General Ranjit Kumar before the Supreme Court regarding promotions of reserved-category employees against unreserved vacancies. [Puncham Singh Vs UoI]. A bench of judicial member Ranjana Shahi and administrative member Lok Ranjan observed that certain sections of the Railways were deliberately attempting to reinterpret judicial pronouncements and the undertaking given by the Solicitor General. The observations came while allowing three applications filed by railway employees challenging the promotion of reserved-category candidates against unreserved vacancies. The dispute concerned whether employees who had entered service through reservation or obtained promotions against reserved vacancies could subsequently claim promotion against unreserved posts on the basis of their own merit. The tribunal noted that in September 2016, then Solicitor General Ranjit Kumar had assured the Supreme Court that the government would not make further promotions of reserved-category employees against unreserved vacancies by relying on two circulars issued in 2010. The assurance was given during contempt proceedings in Samta Andolan Samiti v. Sanjay Kothari , arising from litigation concerning reservation in promotions. Following the hearing on September 29, 2016, Kumar wrote to the government explaining the undertaking and warning that its violation would invite contempt proceedings. The tribunal reproduced his communication, in which Kumar stated: " The Government would not pass any further order of promotion relying upon either of these two circulars or on the basis thereof ." The communication further warned that any violation of the assurance would bring about "a definite contempt". Consequently, the Railway Board issued instructions on September 30, 2016, holding its earlier circular in abeyance. items.title: CCPA imposes ₹1 lakh penalty on Shangri-La Eros for levying service charge on restaurant bills
items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹1 lakh on Shangri-La Eros hotel in New Delhi for levying service charges on restaurant bills despite the Delhi High Court ruling that such charges must be voluntary. A coram comprising Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra held that adding default service charges to bills and putting the burden on customers to request removal of such charges violate consumer rights and amount to unfair trade practice. The CCPA observed that merely describing a charge as optional did not make its collection voluntary when the amount was automatically included in the bill. " Merely displaying the collection of non-statutory charge like 'service charge', on the menu card or on the bill does not cure the underlying compulsion ," the Authority said. The October 22 order arose from consumer complaints received in May and June 2025 alleging that Mister Chai, a restaurant at Shangri-La Eros, had imposed a 10 percent service charge on food bills. The complaints prompted a preliminary inquiry followed by an investigation by the CCPA's Director General (Investigation). The investigation found that the restaurant had levied a service charge of ₹435 on a bill of ₹4,350 in May 2025. In another instance, a service charge of ₹125 was imposed on a bill of ₹1,250 in June 2025. The investigation concluded that automatically adding such charges created a misleading impression that their payment was compulsory. items.title: Supreme Court too Chief Justice-centric, encourages ‘hero worship’: Former Justice AS Oka
items.summary: Hero worship of the Chief Justice of India stems from the concentration of too much power in the office, said former Supreme Court judge Justice Abhay S Oka on Tuesday. Justice Oka made the observation in a keynote address he gave at a seminar on “Accountability of Judges” organised by the Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reforms (CJAR). "Look at the Supreme Court... most of the administrative decisions are taken by only the Chief Justice of India. And so Chief Justice controls most of the administrative functions of the Supreme Court... because of this, all powerful position of the Chief Justice, sometimes stakeholders indulge in hero worship of Chief Justice of India," said Justice Oka. He said that such a concentration of power was a concern that had also been raised by Dr BR Ambedkar during the Constituent Assembly debates. "He (Dr BR Ambedkar) had warned all of us about serious consequence of hero worship. Because hero worship comes from absolute power concentrated in the hands of the Chief Justice of India," noted Justice Oka. Justice AS Oka Because of this, all powerful position of the Chief Justice, sometimes stakeholders indulge in hero worship of Chief Justice of India. He added that the Supreme Court needed a proper roster system to prevent manual intervention in the allocation of cases to benches. He observed that the Supreme Court currently assigns the same categories of cases to multiple Benches, leaving litigants and lawyers uncertain about which Bench would hear a particular matter. Justice Oka argued that a clear roster system, similar to those followed by High Courts, would improve transparency and accountability. items.title: Delhi High Court upholds 7-year jail term for 5 men convicted in Delhi riots case
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday upheld the trial court order sentencing five men to seven years' imprisonment for culpable homicide over the death of a 22-year-old man during the 2020 Delhi riots. Justice Madhu Jain dismissed the appeal filed by convicts Aman Kashyap, Devinder Kumar, Pradeep Rai, Ashish @ Goli and Arun Kumar against their conviction. The High Court ruled that the evidence showed “more than the mere presence” of the appellants in a crowd. “The common judgment of conviction dated 30.11.2024 and order on sentence dated 13.01.2025 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-03, North-East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, in Sessions Case No. 199/2021, arising out of FIR No. 87/2020 registered at Police Station Dayalpur, are upheld insofar as the present appellants are concerned,” Justice Jain concluded. Justice Madhu Jain The five men were convicted by the trial court under Sections 148 (rioting while armed with a deadly weapon) and 304 Part I (culpable homicide) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Notably, the case arose from an FIR registered at the Dayalpur police station after a man, identified as Monish, was allegedly chased and assaulted by a mob near Brijpuri on February 25, 2020. Monish later died in the hospital. The convicts argued that the prosecution's case suffered from inconsistencies in eyewitness accounts, delays in recording police witnesses' statements and the absence of a test identification parade. Rejecting the challenge, the High Court relied on the testimony of a police constable who identified the five men as being at the forefront of the armed mob and allegedly exhorting others to assault Monish. The court also considered the accounts of other police personnel who described the pursuit and assault before the injured man was rescued. It observed that the absence of a test identification parade did not automatically invalidate identification evidence. Advocates Faraz Anees and Kartik Vashisht appeared for the convicts. Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) Rajat Nair with advocates Dhruv Pande, Imon Bhattacharya and Sarthak represented the State. [Read Judgement]

items.title: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall near Andhra coast, brings destructive winds and heavy rain
items.summary: Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab continued to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28 morning, bringing destructive winds and torrential rain that uprooted trees, damaged electricity infrastructure and inundated low-lying areas. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the landfall process was expected to continue for several more hours. The storm began crossing the coast in the early hours of October 28, near the stretch between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam. The IMD reported sustained wind speeds of 125 to 135 kmph, with gusts reaching 150 kmph. Its northern spiral band had moved further inland, while the centre remained close to the coastline. North coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded extremely heavy rainfall overnight. Kannuripalem in Anakapalli district received around 263 mm of rain in the 24 hours ending at 8 am on October 28, according to the state Directorate of Economics and Statistics. Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district recorded a similar amount, while a police battalion campus in Visakhapatnam received around 260 mm. Thirty-nine automatic weather stations across Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam and Vizianagaram districts recorded more than 204.5 mm of rain, the threshold the IMD uses for extremely heavy rainfall. Within Visakhapatnam city, Simhachalam received around 238 mm and Madhurawada around 207 mm. The storm’s impact was reported across the coastal districts, including Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam, East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna. Preliminary reports indicated damage to crops, uprooted trees and electricity poles, and power outages in several areas. Low-lying parts of Dr BR Ambedkar Konaseema district were inundated. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the situation through a teleconference involving around 32,000 officials and field personnel. He also held a meeting with senior officials from the electricity, irrigation, roads and buildings, agriculture, urban development and panchayat raj departments to assess the damage and coordinate relief measures. Naidu directed officials to prepare preliminary estimates of crop losses and communicate the state’s response to the Union government. He also instructed them to clear fallen trees from roads within two hours, restore electricity once high-speed winds subside and ensure that cyclone shelters have adequate food, drinking water and medical facilities. items.title: Telangana: Senior IAS officer Jayesh Ranjan to seek voluntary retirement
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Senior IAS officer Jayesh Ranjan has said that he plans to seek voluntary retirement from civil services nine months ahead of his scheduled retirement. Jayesh is currently serving as Special Chief Secretary for Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority Area (HMDA). Speaking to TNM, Jayesh said that he will be applying for VRS in January 2027, ahead of his actual retirement in September. “I have nothing planned as things stand but I'm looking for opportunities beyond government work,” he said. His exit comes months after he was considered for the post of Telangana Chief Secretary in June 2026. The Congress led Telangana government ultimately appointed Sanjay Jaju to the position. Jayesh’s recent career has been marked by a series of changes in responsibilities. In December 2025, the Telangana government reassigned him from his role as Special Chief Secretary and CEO of the Industry and Investment Cell in the Chief Minister’s Office to head the Metropolitan Area and Urban Development portfolio covering the HMDA region. The reshuffle, announced on December 25, also saw him retain additional responsibilities as Special Chief Secretary for Youth Advancement, Tourism and Culture (YAT&C), Sports, and Director of Archaeology. Meanwhile, K Ramakrishna Rao continued as Special Chief Secretary and CEO of the Foreign Affairs Committee (FAC) for the Industry and Investment Cell, as well as the Smart Proactive Efficient and Effective Delivery (SPEED) initiative. These changes followed another significant reshuffle in April 2025, when Jayesh was moved out of the Industries and Information Technology portfolio. Rao took over that assignment, while Jayesh was given responsibilities in the Chief Minister’s Office, including leadership of the Industry and Investment Cell and SPEED. items.title: Palestinian citizens face a painful choice in Israel’s election: To vote or not
items.summary: Elections are typically framed as a choice for voters. For Palestinian citizens of Israel, however, the country’s national ballots pose more of a dilemma. Constituting about one-sixth of eligible voters in Israel, Palestinian citizens could hold the difference in a race expected to be close . But voting involves a trade-off: By casting a ballot for their best interests, many Palestinian citizens believe they also risk legitimizing a process that seeks to silence their voice and a system that treats their citizenship as conditional . The coming Israeli election on Oct. 27, 2026 , brings that tension to a new peak. Since the last general election in 2022 , the destruction and mass killing in Gaza , restrictions on Palestinian citizens’ speech and protest and leading opposition parties’ rejection of having Arab political partners have sharpened the dilemma of seeking protection through institutions that reinforce their exclusion. Having devoted most of my academic career to studying relations between Israel and its Palestinian citizens , I see the question facing Palestinian citizens of Israel as part of a much longer struggle over survival, citizenship and political belonging. Citizenship as protection The approximate 1.7 million Palestinian citizens of Israel – out of a total population of around 10 million Israeli citizens and 15 million people living under Israeli direct or indirect control – are largely the descendants of Arabs who stayed on land that became the state of Israel. The category excludes the descendants of 750,000 Palestinians who were forced from their homes during the Arab-Israeli war of 1948 – most of whom were prevented from returning. A hurried wartime census dated Nov. 8, 1948, helped determine who would be recognized as belonging to the new state. Registration and subsequent citizenship requirements excluded anyone who was absent from their home at the time of the census. This included Palestinians who had sought temporary shelter in neighboring countries or elsewhere in what was Mandatory Palestine. Therefore, the census did more than count residents: In most cases, Palestinians displaced by the war who were absent when it was conducted were excluded from the population register . That made it almost impossible for them to obtain citizenship and return to their homes. items.title: Israeli election: why nobody has been talking about Palestinian statehood
items.summary: As Israelis head to the polls on October 27 one major issue that has not received serious attention during the campaign is Israel’s flat rejection of Palestinian statehood. This puts Israel seriously at odds with world opinion. As it stands, 159 countries around the world recognise Palestinian statehood , including diplomatic heavyweights such as the UK and France . The two UN security council members joined Australia, Andorra, Canada, Luxembourg, Malta, Monaco, Portugal and San Marino in formally recognising the state of Palestine in September 2025. This represents an important shift within the world’s most important diplomatic frameworks. Now, nearly half of the G7 and four of the five permanent members of the UN security council – China, France, Russia and the UK – recognise Palestine as a legitimate state. This international pressure was recently ramped up by international sanctions by the UK and others against Israeli settler groups. Given this pressure – as well as the ongoing conflict in Gaza – you’d expect opposition parties, at least, to engage with the record of the Netanyahu government on the Palestinian question. But there is silence. Not only from the government, but also from the opposition parties hoping to replace it. The political parties comprising the ultra-nationalist government of the incumbent Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, champion “destroying Hamas”. They continue to flatly reject the notion of Palestinian statehood – to the contrary, they enthusiastically promote the expansion of Israeli settlements . Netanyahu’s extreme-right partners, who he has depended on to keep him in power, include the Religious Zionism party of finance minister Belazel Smotrich, and national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power. These two parties want to go further. Their election campaign advocates the occupation of the whole of the West Bank. They back this with a euphemistically branded plan for “voluntary Palestinian emigration”. The key contenders to replace Netanyahu are Gadi Eisenkot , the leader of Yashar (Straight), and Naftali Bennet , the leader of B'Yachad (Together). They have diverged from the Netanyahu government’s policy by promising to bring order to the West Bank by curbing settler violence. They both reject the idea of expanding settlements and promoting Palestinian emigration. items.title: Rough waves disrupt Ennore Expressway in Chennai as Cyclone Arnab hits AP
items.summary: Rough waves driven by Cyclone Arnab surged over the shoreline and onto the Ennore Expressway in north Chennai on the evening of October 27, disrupting traffic, pushing vehicles off the road and sweeping away roadside stalls. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has now closed the affected stretch of the Ennore Expressway. Videos circulating on social media showed cars, autorickshaws and two-wheelers being drenched by waves, while some smaller vehicles were pushed by the water’s force. The Ennore Expressway connects Ennore with Kasimedu harbour and is used by trucks travelling to the port as well as residents of Kasimedu, Tollgate, Thiruvottiyur and Ennore. Police diverted traffic to prevent accidents. According to Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC), vehicles travelling from Ramakrishna Nagar to Annai Sivagami Nagar were directed via Ernavur Bridge, Murugar Kovil Road and Kathivakkam Beach. Vehicles from Thazhakuppam and Ennore were diverted via Kathivakkam Bridge and Murugar Kovil Road. The disruption in Chennai came as Cyclone Arnab, classified as a very severe cyclonic storm, began crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast in the early hours of October 28. Several coastal settlements in north Chennai including Bharathiyar Nagar, Burma Nagar, Nettukuppam, Thalankuppam, Indira Gandhi Kuppam, Periyakuppam and Chinnakuppam experienced impacts. Seawater entered parts of Thalankuppam but receded before reaching nearby houses and fishers in Kasi Kovil Kuppam in Thiruvottiyur reported seawater entering their homes. Thiruvottiyur MLA N Senthil Kumar visited the affected area and said there was no need for the public to panic. Despite the alarming conditions, some youths were seen climbing onto coastal rocks to take selfies and record videos for social media. Police were deployed to issue warnings and disperse crowds. The Indian Coast Guard has also been conducting reviews for the past two days to ensure that fishing boats return to shore amid Sea State 6 conditions, classified as very rough. Such conditions can generate waves measuring four to six metres (13–20 feet), posing serious risks to small boats, and larger ships can also experience substantial rolling and pitching. The northern Chennai coastline has a relatively narrow belt, with some stretches measuring barely 20–30 metres or less. Groynes have been constructed along parts of the coast to help withstand waves reaching the shoreline.

items.title: In opting for Lula, Brazil made a conservative choice to elect a man of the left over one of the far right
items.summary: The 2026 elections in Brazil played out amid an widespread assumption repeated around the world : that the country was polarized and that would inform the vote. But the word “polarization” implies symmetry – and symmetry is something that never existed in the contest between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. On one side, a moderate center-left politician with a center-right running mate, Geraldo Alckmin. On the other, a representative of the radical right and a member of an international movement that critics say threatens democracies around the world. Flávio is no mere conservative. While he may be courted and supported by the members of the Republican Party in the U.S., his policies put him more in the mold of Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany and Portugal’s Enough, a party that advocates the repatriation of immigrants and a ban on Muslim places of worship. On the day he launched his candidacy, at an event of Brazil’s Liberal Party (PL) in São Paulo, Flávio laid out three of the guiding principles of what his administration would look like. First was the so called “Project Darkness”, a crime-fighting plan inspired by by El Salvador’s hard-right President Nayib Bukele . Second was joining the Shield of the Americas , U.S. President Donald Trump’s military and political initiative for the continent. Thirdly, Flávio laid out plans for the “tesouraço” or “big cut” – a slashing of public spending modeled after Argentinian President Javier Milei’s “ chainsaw ” economic policy. Since he didn’t provide any details, it’s unclear whether it would be just as sharp as Milei’s, but it was enough to strike fear into those who depend on social programs to survive. Milei himself was at the launch event. He arrived singing the song The Panic Show by the Argentine hard rock band La Renga. Flávio accompanied Milei in the song’s refrain: “Yo soy el león, soy el rey y te destrozaré” (“I am the lion, I am the king, and I will tear you apart”) while dancing along with the Argentine president. It is, I believe, the form, more than the content, that defines the members of the far-right brotherhood that threatens democracies around the world. items.title: Police file case after Mangaluru medical college students allege ragging, threats
items.summary: A 21-year-old student from Kollam has accused seniors at Kanachur Medical College in Mangaluru of repeatedly ragging him and his classmates, confining them in a hotel room and threatening them with violence. Ullal police have registered a case following the complaint, and seven students have been issued notices, according to reports. The complainant is a first-year BSc Neuroscience Technology student at the college in Deralakatte. His complaint describes three incidents on October 2, October 15 and October 22, involving alleged threats, forced singing and the humiliation of a junior student. On October 2, senior students Ashab and Asfaq allegedly confronted the complainant near a restaurant opposite the college after he went outside the campus without wearing his uniform. One of them threatened to break his limbs and said he would complain to the college authorities, according to the complaint. On October 15, Ashab allegedly called the student repeatedly and asked him and six classmates to meet near the Clock Tower. The group was then taken to a room at a nearby hotel and prevented from leaving until they sang songs, the complaint alleged. Ashab allegedly recorded their performance on his mobile phone and circulated the video among other students. The complaint further alleged that the seniors threatened to target a junior student every day and warned that anyone who reported the incidents would have their limbs broken and be sent to a graveyard. Ullal police have registered a case against Ashab, Asfaq and others. The investigation is under way.
